**B. Fee simple subject to condition subsequent.** The grant uses "provided, however, that if... then the grantor... may re-enter," which is the classic wording of a power of termination. The estate does not end automatically, so the grantor must act to cut it short. A fee simple determinable would instead use durational language like "so long as" or "until" and revert automatically. That is why my earlier answer of A was wrong, and the team note's "automatic" reading doesn't fit the re-entry wording.

CONFIDENCE: 85
